transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is that most nights, once my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen. I just... I end up eating way past a normal plate. If there are leftovers from an event or something, like fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls, whatever is in there... I'll just eat until a whole tray is empty, or half the fridge is just gone.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these late-night episodes?

Yeah, that's exactly it. It's like... once I take that first bite, the decision has already been made for me. Even while I’m standing there literally telling myself, 'George, stop now,' it doesn't matter. My hands just keep fixing another plate or opening another container. I just can't seem to make myself stop once I start.
Do you feel like you have no control over your eating during these episodes?

Yeah, exactly like I was just saying. There's just zero control. My mind is telling me to quit, but my body just ignores it and goes for the next container anyway. It really feels like the choice is entirely out of my hands the second I take that first bite.
Do these episodes of eating late at night happen when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset?
No, not really. I mean, I guess I get stressed sometimes like anyone else, but I wouldn't say that's what sets it off. It just happens whether it's been a good day or a bad day.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed after these late-night eating episodes?

Yeah, very much so. Afterward, I just... I feel sick with myself. People see me as this organized, strong guy, but then I'm just sitting there completely ashamed and guilty. I get so disgusted with myself that I let it happen all over again.
Do you feel like you're eating really fast during these late-night episodes?

Yeah, I do. I eat so fast during those times that I barely even taste it. I used to take a lot of pride in cooking and enjoying my food, but late at night... I'm just standing at the kitchen counter, swallowing big bites before I've even finished chewing the last one. It's just a rush to get it down.
Do you remember everything that happens during these late-night eating episodes?
Yeah, I remember all of it. I... it's not like I black out or anything. I know exactly what I'm doing and what I'm eating the whole time. I'm fully awake, I just... can't seem to stop myself.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over time due to these eating episodes?
I'm not really sure, honestly. I don't... I don't really step on the scale or keep track of my weight. So I haven't noticed any specific changes.
During these episodes, do you think you're eating an amount of food that's significantly more than what most people would eat under normal circumstances?

Yeah, definitely. Most nights when my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen, and... I eat way past a normal plate. I mean, I'll go through fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls... just whatever event leftovers are in there. I'll keep going until a whole tray is empty, or like half the fridge is just gone. So, yeah, it's a lot more than what anyone would normally eat.
Do you usually try to hide or conceal the evidence of your late-night eating from your wife or others?

No, I don't really try to hide it. I mean, the food is just gone the next day. She knows I ate it. I don't go out of my way to bury the containers in the trash or anything like that. It's just... I eat it, and the empty trays are sitting right there in the fridge or the sink in the morning.
Do you ever eat in response to feeling emotional, such as when you're bored, happy, or upset?

No, I wouldn't really say so. I don't think it has anything to do with my mood. It's not like I'm sitting there feeling upset or bored and then go to the kitchen because of that. It just... I just end up eating regardless of what kind of day I've had or how I'm feeling.
Do you feel like something is compelling you to continue eating during these episodes, beyond just your own desire or lack of willpower?

Yeah, I do. It's like... once I take that first bite, it just feels like the decision has already been made for me. I'll actually be standing there telling myself, "George, stop now," but my hands just keep fixing another plate or opening another container. I just can't seem to stop myself once I start.
Do you ever find yourself eating when you're feeling emotional, such as anxious, happy, or upset?

I think I just mentioned this a minute ago, but... no, not really. It doesn't seem to have much to do with my mood. Anxious, happy, upset... it doesn't really matter. Like I said, I just end up eating either way, regardless of how I'm feeling that day.
How often do these late-night eating episodes happen?
For months now, honestly... I can’t think of a single week where it didn’t happen at least once. And most weeks, it’s been several nights. Usually it happens right after my wife goes to bed.
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or a trance while you're eating during these late-night episodes?

No, I wouldn't say it's like a trance. I'm fully awake and aware of what I'm doing. Like I was saying before, I'm actually telling myself to stop while I'm doing it. So I'm definitely not spaced out or anything, I just... I just can't seem to make myself stop.
Do you ever find yourself eating when you're not hungry but are feeling emotional?

Well, like I mentioned a few minutes ago, the emotional part doesn't really factor into it for me. But as far as the hunger goes... yeah, a lot of the time I’m not hungry at all. 

I mean, I might have just eaten a perfectly good dinner with my wife. But later on, I'll still go back into the kitchen and start picking at the leftovers... and then it just turns into another full-on spread. So, I'm definitely doing it even when I'm physically full.
About how many nights in a typical month would you say you have one of these late-night eating episodes?

Well, like I was saying a few minutes ago, I really can't think of a single week for months now where it didn't happen at least once. And most weeks it's several nights, usually right after my wife goes to bed. So if we're looking at a whole month... I guess it would be easily ten to fifteen nights. Maybe even more.
Do you think your late-night eating episodes are ever triggered by emotional events that happened during the day?

Like I was saying just a minute ago, no, I really don't think so. The emotional stuff just doesn't seem to trigger it for me. I could have a completely normal, fine day where nothing bad or stressful happens at all, and I still end up doing it. It just... it happens regardless of how I'm feeling.
